correctness.rationale: For nonzero normal u the difference of squared support functions is (a²−b²)(u₁²−u₂²). The strict cases expose ellipse arcs with gauge one (on the larger-coordinate branch); diagonal normals expose four segments between the stated e and f with coordinate reflections. The first-quadrant contact ratio is b²/a², and the segment is s+t=√(a²+b²), giving the two radial branches with agreement at contact. On each half of a segment q² is strictly convex and the two limiting endpoint values of q are 1 and (a²+b²)/(2ab)>1. Thus only the four face midpoints maximize q on the hull. A normalized sum with positive weights belongs to the hull; equality forces both inputs onto the supporting line, whose only union points are the exposed contacts. Their convex combination equals the midpoint only for equal weights. This also attains the convexification bound, by radial normalization. Zero input is strict when a>b, and a=b gives ordinary Euclidean equality. The frozen script was inspected, not executed; its samples do not prove any universal quantifier.
